evidence.correctness: Recomputed daysUntilDue against an author-independent oracle (Date.UTC day numbers of the Y-M-D strings, no local-time arithmetic) in 9 time zones incl. Hand: 2026-11-19 -> 2027-03-14 = 11+31+31+28+14 = 115, tool 115 (TZ=America/Chicago); 2028-02-28 -> 2028-03-01 = 2 across leap day, tool 2; 2026-03-07 23:59 -> 2026-03-09 across US spring-forward = 2, tool 2. Worked table on the days-remaining page (0/1/7/-1 and urgent/urgent/normal/past-due) reproduced. Readiness: ready iff every listed row is 'ready', blocked counted missing - correct by definition. Computed numbers are right; the defects are in what the page surfaces (ready path hides a past-due deadline) and in the date-only model, scored under claims/domain.

All work. Not delivered: the 'urgency label' the days-remaining page (line 41), index FAQ (line 31), sticky-note page (lines 46, 59, 78) and JobTread page (line 94) describe - assessBid computes `urgency` but index.html never reads it (`grep -n urgency index.html` outside JSON-LD/FAQ: none). evidence.craft: Read model.mjs, share.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html, the four HTML pages and all test files. model.mjs is small and clear. index.html:48 and :66 are 1,000+ character one-line handlers mixing DOM building, assessment and usage. index.html:99-110 is an unreachable branch (the #usage element is always a checkbox) copied from a shared template. share.mjs:39-42 comment says a calendar-invalid date 'is treated as no deadline' by daysUntilDue, but V8 rolls it over: `daysUntilDue('2099-02-30', new Date(2099,1,27,9))` -> 3 (March 2), observed in edges.mjs; the browser date input masks it, the model does not. assessBid would throw on a row missing owner/note (item.owner.trim()).
evidence.claims: Disclaimer (no warranty, not advice) present on all four pages and README; usage tracking present and honestly described (local counters, DNT/GPC). llms.txt source points at duncan-haywood.github.io but served copy (`node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs contractor-bid-readiness` -> 'no placeholder or retired origin left') is rewritten to marisstella.app: source-only, not a defect. JobTread page is fairly framed: no price or plan invented, explicit non-affiliation, describes JobTread only at category level (residential/remodeling construction management: CRM, estimating, budgeting, scheduling, financials) - consistent with JobTread's public positioning, not verified live here; 'JobTread, LLC' entity name not verified (partial). Unbacked: 'add your own deadline to see the count and the urgency label together' (days page:41), 'flags urgent or past-due automatically' (sticky page:59), 'marks the whole submission urgent' (sticky page:78), JobTread page:94 'when does that tip into urgent or past-due? -> This checklist's readiness report' - the report and page never show urgency. 'There is no window where a bid that can no longer be filed is still labeled urgent' (days page:39) is false for any bid with a due time: due 2026-11-19, checked 15:00 after a 14:00 opening -> 0, 'urgent', 'The deadline is today.' (edges.mjs).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: senior estimator lists 12 requirements for a county RFP due 2:00 PM. Works: statuses, owners, Markdown handoff, share link. Breaks in the first hour: (1) nothing is saved - a refresh or closed tab loses every row unless a share link was copied (no storage of rows in index.html); (2) no due time or time zone, so after the bid opening the board still says 'The deadline is today'; (3) all-ready but past-due bid reads 'Ready: all N listed items are marked ready.' with no deadline sentence (index.html:66), and the Markdown report (model.mjs:61) carries no days-remaining or urgency at all; (4) no addenda log, pre-bid/RFI cutoff, sub-bid due dates or a starter list of standard public-bid forms (bid bond, addenda acknowledgment, non-collusion affidavit, DBE/MBE). Usable as a scratch checklist, not as a bid-control record.
evidence.domain: Compared against public-bid practice: solicitations state an exact receipt time and place (e.g. '2:00 PM local time'), and FAR 14.304(b)(1) / most state codes reject any bid received after that exact time; bid managers track addenda acknowledgment, bond, and sub-quote deadlines separately from the bid due time. The tool models the deadline as a calendar date in the viewer's browser time zone, so a remote estimator in another zone and any after-opening check get the wrong state; it has no notion of internal milestones (sub bids due T-24h, pricing freeze). Its whole-day arithmetic itself is right and DST-safe.

defects.what: Deadline is a calendar date only, in the viewer's browser time zone: no due time or issuing-office zone. A bid due today at 2:00 PM checked at 3:00 PM reads 0 days, 'urgent', 'The deadline is today.' - and the days-remaining page claims 'there is no window where a bid that can no longer be filed is still labeled urgent'.

All-ready summary omits the deadline sentence: a bid 9 days past due reads 'Ready: all 1 listed items are marked ready.' with no past-due warning; the Markdown report (model.mjs:61) never includes days remaining or urgency either.
Urgency (urgent/past-due) is computed by assessBid but never rendered; four pages promise an urgency label/flag in the readiness report.

DST regression test only exercises a DST boundary when the runner's TZ observes DST; under default UTC the Math.round -> Math.floor mutant survives. No test drives index.html's summary, and the empty-checklist guard mutant survives.
Checklist rows are not persisted: a refresh or closed tab loses every requirement unless a share link was copied; no beforeunload warning.

Comment claims a calendar-invalid date from a share link is treated as no deadline; daysUntilDue('2099-02-30') returns 3 (rolled to March 2). Masked in the browser by input type=date, wrong in the model.
Share link silently truncates notes over 120 chars and drops rows beyond 100 with no notice to sender or recipient.
Unreachable usage-control branch (button variant) copied from a template; 1,000+ char one-line handlers.

verdict: The day arithmetic is right: an author-independent oracle agreed on 69,174 cases in each of 9 time zones, including zones whose DST change happens at midnight, and three hand counts matched (115 days, 2 across a leap day, 2 across spring-forward). The JobTread comparison is fairly framed and every page carries the disclaimer and honest local usage counting. It does not meet the bar. A bid manager works to a due time, and the tool works to a calendar date in the browser's zone, so after a 2:00 PM bid opening it still says 'The deadline is today' while its own page claims no such window exists. An all-ready bid that is past due reads plainly 'Ready', and the urgency label that four pages promise is computed but never shown. The DST test only works in a DST time zone, and 2 of 4 seeded mutants survived. Rows are lost on refresh. It is usable as a scratch list, not as a bid-control record.
